To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel design using continuous intravenous and intradudeonal infusions of midazolam and voriconazole allows the assessment of the time course of hepatic and intestinal CYP3A inhibition.
we developed a novel design using continuous intravenous and intradudenal infusions of midazolam and voriconazole for mechanistic quantitative assessment of hepatic and intestinal CYP3A inhibition.
the combination of continuous intravenous and intradudenal infusions of a CYP3A probe drug and a CYP3As inhibitor can be used to assess the dynamic inhibition of CYP3A4/5 in the liver and gut wall.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of new study designs for mechanistic quantitative assessment of DDIs.
the development of a novel design for the assessment of CYP3A-mediated drug-drug interactions.
the development of novel study designs for mechanistic quantitative assessment of DDIs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the novel study design was successful in terms of providing a semiphysiological pharmacokinetic model for the quantification of the dynamic CYP3A inhibition by VRZ in the intestine and the liver.
the model developed is able to capture the time-dependent changes in the extent of inhibition of CYP3A by voriconazole in both the gut wall and liver.
the model developed is a useful tool for the assessment of CYP3A-mediated DDIs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed design and analysis method is feasible for a more mechanistic assessment of CYP3A inhibition.
the proposed design and analysis method are suitable for quantifying the extent of CYP3A inhibition by a CYP3A probe drug.

a combination of intravenous infusion of midazolam and intraduodenally infused midazolam with voriconazole, administered as a continuous intravenous infusion, provides a novel study design to investigate the dynamic inhibition of CYP3A4 by voriconazole in the gut and liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of continuous infusions in the assessment of DDIs is a promising strategy for a more accurate quantification of inhibition and for the identification of the underlying mechanisms.
a combination of intravenous infusion of substrate and inhibitor with intraduodenally infused substrate can provide a more accurate and precise estimate of DDIs.
a novel study design combining intravenous and intradudenal infusions of substrate and inhibitor allows for a more accurate assessment for DDIs occurring in gut wall and liver.
